note: Hand-curated Python package -> C++ library. fit: good = drop-in shape, partial = same job with different semantics, none = no equivalent worth handing to a port (blocks the unit). Unknown packages are reported as unknown, never guessed.

python.note: callbacks and error handling differ; keep the HTTP semantics in one place
async model differs (coroutines/executors vs asyncio)
routing exists; templating and extensions do not
no automatic OpenAPI or dependency injection
ORM, admin and template stack has no single C++ counterpart
process model and reloading differ
tags and unsafe loaders differ
filters and inheritance differ
help text and exit codes must be recorded, not assumed
validation errors are messages; record them
dtype promotion, broadcasting and layout differ
special functions and sparse solvers have no single equivalent
index semantics and NaN handling differ
plotting is not a library port; keep the charts or the data
resampling and colour conversions differ
use the C++ API of the same runtime; do not reimplement kernels
no drop-in; estimates must be re-validated, not ported blindly
ORM identity map and lazy loading have no equivalent
driver semantics differ
service coverage and pagination differ
generate from the same .proto
construction APIs and defaults differ
parsing grammar and DST rules differ
namespaces and serialisation differ
HTML error recovery differs
error messages differ
lookaround and \w semantics differ; record real patterns
formatters and handlers differ
terminal detection differs
the recorded cases are the suite; C++ tests cover what recording cannot
the event loop is the app's architecture, not a dependency
GIL-shaped code does not port structurally
UI stays in Python: keep this unit and port what it calls
